clue.text: Fluid — litre: one pound

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A label or recipe line listing a quantity of fluid: a litre, priced at one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: QUID is everyday British slang for one pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a substance that flows freely is described with either word, as noun or adjective.

clue.text: Key cricketer, one'll take off cap

definitions.meaning: something that unlocks or gives access, as a key does
a batsman who starts the innings for a cricket side
a bottle tool that removes the metal cap

explanation.surface: An important cricketer who will doff his cap to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a key opens things, a cricket side's opening batsman starts the innings, and a bottle tool prises off caps. The surface reads 'Key' as an adjective, 'important'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense names something that begins or unlocks: a door key, a lead-off batsman, a bottle tool.

clue.text: Big clock next to old penny in corner

parts.note: Big Ben is the great clock bell at Westminster, so the clock gives its other word
D (from Latin denarius) was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimalisation

explanation.surface: A huge clock sits beside an old coin tucked away in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big clock' supplies only BEN, the second word of Big Ben, London's famous clock bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a turn in a road or river is a corner taken by traffic.

clue.text: After ten whipped up, cake topping is tempting

indicators.note: the topping is placed after the rearranged ten in the answer
whipping up beats and mixes, so the letters of ten are stirred into a new order

parts.note: icing is the sugary coating spread on top of a cake

explanation.surface: Once ten things are whipped up, the cake topping looks delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The baking surface makes 'whipped up' look like beating cream, but it rearranges the word ten; 'After' puts the topping second.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something alluring or appealing draws you in, just as a tempting offer does.

clue.text: Hero of poem a wit, ha-ha, misrepresented

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are presented in a different order

explanation.surface: The hero of a poem is mocked as 'a wit, ha-ha', a misleading portrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges the eight letters of A WIT HAHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Native American hero of Longfellow's 1855 narrative poem The Song of Hiawatha.

clue.text: Catalogue Hungarian composer for the listener

indicators.note: a listener hears the composer's name, so the clue wants a word that sounds the same; the letters also sitting at the start of the word listener is a coincidence

parts.note: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian piano virtuoso and composer

explanation.surface: A record company catalogues the works of a Hungarian composer for its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the listener' signals a soundalike of LISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a catalogue is an itemised record or register of things.

clue.text: Son on board plane makes joke

indicators.note: being on board a plane means being inside it, so one letter goes within the aircraft word

parts.note: a jet is a jet-engined aeroplane

explanation.surface: A boy on an aeroplane cracks a joke to pass the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts S inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a jest is a funny remark or quip made to amuse.

clue.text: Flight impressed Egypt's leader

parts.note: to impress a mark on something is to stamp it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An escape impressed Egypt's ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter of 'Egypt's'. 'Flight' looks like air travel but means a headlong rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a panicked mass rush of animals or people running away is a flight.

clue.text: Adult males use four-letter words, such as vest, suit, and ties!

parts.note: men are adult males
four-letter words are obscenities, so using them is to swear

explanation.surface: Grown men curse, rattling off four-letter words like vest, suit and ties.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: vest, suit and ties are themselves four-letter words, but innocent ones. 'such as' links them to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples: a vest, a suit and ties are items of clothing sold for men.

clue.text: Black toy daughter lost

indicators.note: the daughter is lost, so her letter is taken away

parts.note: Dinky toys are a classic British brand of die-cast model cars

explanation.surface: A child's black toy goes missing, and so does the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes D from DINKY; Dinky toys are well-known British die-cast model vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something stained or coloured as dark as ink is very dark, pitch black.

clue.text: Large square Italian dish containing apples, primarily

indicators.note: the dish holds the next letter within it

parts.note: pizza is the well-known Italian flatbread dish

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter of apples

explanation.surface: A big Italian pizza with apples on it, mainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives A, and 'containing' places it inside PIZZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an Italian open public plaza or town square, often large.

clue.text: Select sweet with no centre

indicators.note: the middle letter of the sweet's name is removed

parts.note: a choc ice is a block of ice cream coated in chocolate, a British treat

explanation.surface: Choose a chocolate with no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate; 'with no centre' removes its middle letter, the second C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something select is of the best quality, as prime cuts are described.

clue.text: Female and I live in the home

parts.note: to live in a place is to reside there

explanation.surface: A woman says she and the speaker live at home together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live in' together give RESIDE; the definition is 'the home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonym: the hearth area by the fire stands for home and domestic life, as in fireside chats.

clue.text: Wallpaper may be put in one's place?

definitions.meaning: rolls of wallpaper are trimmed to fit the wall literally
an idiom for humbling someone who is getting above themselves

explanation.surface: A decorating note on trimming wallpaper to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal decorating sense sits beside the idiom for deflating someone's self-importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: deflating someone's pride is the figurative sense; trimming a roll to the right dimensions is the literal one.

clue.text: Commercial outlet in period leading up to Christmas

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: A retail outlet runs commercials in the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial' and 'outlet' look like shopping words; here they are a noun for an advert and an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the church season of the four Sundays before Christmas Day.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine's father fencing unlikely trio

indicators.note: fencing something in surrounds it, so the father word goes round the other letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: an unlikely version of trio is an odd, rearranged one

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine's father fencing with an improbable trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges TRIO to ORTI; 'fencing' looks like swordplay but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the clever heiress of The Merchant of Venice, who pleads the quality of mercy.

clue.text: Belgian detective in our hotel, unhappy with price

indicators.note: unhappy letters are in a bad state, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Belgian sleuth staying at our hotel complains about the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' rearranges OUR HOTEL plus PRICE together; 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Agatha Christie's famous fictional Belgian sleuth with the moustache and little grey cells.

clue.text: Article put in study for faculty head

indicators.note: the article goes inside the study word

parts.note: a den is a private study or room for work
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article is placed in the study of a university department head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places A inside DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a university, the senior academic leading a faculty holds this title.

clue.text: Strike, a great success

definitions.meaning: to strike is to give a blow
a smash, such as a chart-topping record

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a blow landed on something, and a popular triumph like a bestselling song.

clue.text: Close associate in team punt

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a punt is a kick of a dropped ball before it lands

explanation.surface: A close friend joins the team for a kick of the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like a flat boat or a bet; here it is a kick in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a companion or assistant who accompanies a leading figure, like a hero's partner.

clue.text: Watch cutter swing

parts.note: to watch is to see
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Watch a cutting tool swing back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swing' is a verb: to move up and down or alternate between positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to oscillate back and forth or waver between options, as on a playground plank.

clue.text: A fair representation across "Cape" continent

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across, so they surround the next letter
a representation of the words a fair reshapes them, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A balanced depiction spanning a continent from the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges A FAIR to AFRIA, and 'across' places it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the large landmass south of Europe, one of the world's major continents.

clue.text: Leave former partner on the thing

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: Walk away from an ex who is on about something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts EX above IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go out of or depart from a place.
